stream.accessLost: Access to the stream was lost (session or permission changed).
stream.info: Live means updates arrive. After a dropped connection Studio reconnects by itself and continues where it stopped. Disconnected means it stopped trying: choose Reconnect.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.description: Background jobs of this product: status, attempts, errors and results. Jobs run at least once; handlers must be idempotent.
jobs.kindHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and _ . : - (for example reports.send). Kinds starting with “axentra.” are reserved. A worker must have a handler for this kind.
jobs.priorityHelp: -100 to 100; higher runs first. There is no FIFO guarantee.
jobs.delayHelp: Run no earlier than this many seconds from now.
jobs.maxAttemptsHelp: 1 to 100; empty uses the server default.
jobs.payloadHelp: A JSON object of at most 64 KB. Do not put secrets here: pass ids and read secrets inside the handler.
jobs.idempotencyKeyHelp: Sending the same request again with this key (same kind and tenant) returns the existing job instead of a new one.
jobs.enqueueDescription: Adds a job to the queue. It runs when a worker with a handler for its kind claims it.
jobs.liveHelp: Follows the jobs stream and refreshes the list and counters when jobs change.
jobs.emptyBody: Jobs appear here when your product, a schedule or a webhook enqueues them.
jobs.retryBody: “{{kind}}” ({{id}}) is queued again with its attempts reset to 0. The handler runs again, so it must be idempotent.
jobs.cancelQueuedBody: “{{kind}}” ({{id}}) has not started yet and is cancelled at once.
jobs.cancelRunningBody: “{{kind}}” ({{id}}) is running. Cancellation is requested; the handler stops at its next check. If it finishes first, the job counts as succeeded.
jobs.cancelRequestedToast: Cancellation requested; the running handler stops at its next check
jobs.cancelRequestedNotice: Cancellation was requested. The job ends as cancelled when its handler notices, or as succeeded if it finishes its work first.

stats.title: Overview
stats.last24h: Last 24 hours: {{succeeded}} succeeded, {{failed}} failed or dead.
stats.noneQueued: Nothing is waiting in the queue.

detail.lastErrorHelp: Stored redacted by the server: tokens, keys and connection strings are removed.
detail.redactedHelp: Sensitive values are redacted by the server.
detail.skippedBody: The worker did not run this job because its product is archived or its tenant is suspended (or one of them no longer exists). Jobs fired by a schedule end this way too. The job is kept: once the product and tenant are active again, retry it if it is still needed.

jobs.statusInfo: Failed: the handler reported a permanent error, so there are no more automatic attempts. Dead: every attempt ended with an error. You can retry both.
jobs.attemptsInfo: Every run counts as an attempt. After an error the job waits (2, 4, 8 … seconds with default settings) and runs again, until the maximum is reached and it becomes dead.
jobs.kindInfo: Workers only take kinds they have a handler for. A job whose kind no running worker handles stays queued and never fails, so check the spelling.
jobs.payloadInfo: The payload is stored as entered and is readable for everyone who can view jobs. Fields named like password, secret or token are only hidden in the display.
jobs.priorityInfo: Priority only decides which due job a free worker takes first. It does not interrupt running jobs and does not guarantee an order.
jobs.maxAttemptsInfo: After an error the job is retried with a growing wait. When the last attempt fails it becomes dead and stays in the list, so you can read the error and retry it.
jobs.idempotencyKeyInfo: Studio fills in a new random key each time you open this dialog, so a double click enqueues only once. The same key with a different payload or priority is refused.
jobs.skipped: Not run: product or tenant inactive

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.description: Enqueue jobs at fixed intervals or on cron times (UTC). Each time slot fires at most once; missed slots are combined into one run.
schedules.name: Name
schedules.formDescription: The schedule enqueues a job of this kind with this payload in every slot. A worker must run for schedules to fire.
schedules.kindHelp: The job kind to enqueue, for example reports.send. Kinds starting with “axentra.” are reserved.
schedules.tenantHelp: Optional: enqueue the jobs in this tenant. Cannot be changed later.
schedules.cronHelp: 5 fields in UTC: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. Allowed: *, numbers, ranges (1-5), lists (1,15) and steps (*/10). Day of week 0-7, 0 and 7 are Sunday. No names or macros.
schedules.nextRunHint: The server computes the next run when you save.
schedules.enabledHelp: Disabled schedules keep their settings but do not fire. When enabled again, they continue with the next slot; missed slots are not run.
schedules.deleteBody: “{{name}}” stops firing. Jobs it already enqueued are not affected.
schedules.emptyBody: Create a schedule to run a job regularly.
schedules.timingInfo: Schedules run in UTC, without daylight saving time. Next run and last run are shown in your own time zone.
schedules.intervalInfo: Intervals are counted from 1 January 1970, 00:00 UTC, not from when you save. Every 15 minutes fires at :00, :15, :30 and :45; every day fires at 00:00 UTC.
schedules.cronInfo: UTC, with no daylight saving adjustment: 09:00 in Berlin is 0 8 * * * in winter and 0 7 * * * in summer. If both day of month and day of week are set, a day matches when either one matches.

validation.jsonObject: Enter a JSON object, for example {"report": "monthly"}.

kind.invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and _ . : -, starting with a letter (at most 100 characters).
kind.reserved: Kinds starting with “axentra.” are reserved for Axentra.

type.invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and _ . : -, starting with a letter (at most 150 characters).
type.reserved: Types starting with “axentra.” are reserved for Axentra.

validation.typeFilter: Enter an exact type or a prefix ending in * (for example invoice.*).
validation.patterns: Patterns use lowercase letters, digits, _ . : - and * as wildcard.
validation.interval: The interval must be between {{min}} seconds and {{max}} seconds (366 days).

url.invalid: Enter a complete URL such as https://example.com/hooks.
url.scheme: Only https:// (or http:// on development servers) is allowed.
url.credentials: The URL must not contain a user name or password.
url.fragment: The URL must not contain a fragment (#…).

cron.fieldCount: A cron expression has 5 fields separated by spaces; this one has {{count}}.
cron.syntax: The {{field}} field contains an invalid value: {{value}}
cron.range: Values in the {{field}} field must be between {{min}} and {{max}}.

events.title: Events
events.description: Events published by your product, in the log or live as they happen.
events.typeFilterHelp: Exact type or a prefix ending in *.
events.typeHelp: For example invoice.created. Types starting with “axentra.” are reserved.
events.emptyBody: Events appear here when your product publishes them.
events.publishDescription: Publishes an event in a tenant. Subscribers and matching webhooks receive it.
events.actorInfo: Who published the event: user, api_key or system (Axentra or your product's own code), followed by its id.
events.publishInfo: A published event is real: matching webhook endpoints and your product's subscribers receive it. Use test data and a tenant meant for testing.

live.typesHelp: Optional patterns, separated by commas (for example invoice.*, user.created). Empty: all types.
live.note: Shows events published from now on. While paused the connection stays open and new events are collected. After a dropped connection the stream resumes where it stopped.
live.emptyBody: New events appear here as soon as they are published.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Endpoints that receive signed HTTP requests for events. Deliveries are retried and happen at least once; receivers should deduplicate by event id.
webhooks.urlHelp: HTTPS endpoint that accepts POST requests. Private and local addresses are refused by the server.
webhooks.httpWarning: Plain http:// is only accepted by servers outside production that explicitly allow it.
webhooks.eventTypesHelp: Exact types or patterns with *, for example invoice.* or * for all. Press Enter to add.
webhooks.tenantFilterHelp: Optional: only deliver events of this tenant. Cannot be changed later.
webhooks.enabledHelp: Disabled endpoints receive no new deliveries. Deliveries still waiting for a retry end as dead.
webhooks.createDescription: Axentra generates a signing secret for the endpoint and shows it once.
webhooks.emptyBody: Create an endpoint to send events to another system.
webhooks.secretUsage: Verify the Axentra-Signature header with this secret (the complete value, including whsec_): HMAC-SHA256 over “<t>.<raw body>”, compared in constant time with each v1 value; reject timestamps more than about 5 minutes off.
webhooks.rotateBody: A new secret for {{url}} is generated and shown once. With a grace period, requests are signed with both secrets until it ends.
webhooks.graceHelp: How long the previous secret stays valid.
webhooks.graceUntil: Requests carry signatures with the new and the previous secret until
webhooks.graceActive: Requests carry signatures with the new and the previous secret.
webhooks.disabledNotice: This endpoint is disabled and receives no new deliveries.
webhooks.deleteBody: {{url}} receives no more deliveries, and its delivery history is deleted. To pause the endpoint instead, disable it.
webhooks.urlInfo: The host must resolve to public addresses only; localhost and private networks are refused. Redirects are not followed, and the receiver must answer with a 2xx status within 10 seconds.
webhooks.eventTypesInfo: An event is delivered when it matches any pattern. * stands for any text, so invoice.* covers invoice.created and invoice.paid. Up to 50 patterns.
webhooks.graceInfo: During the grace period every request carries two signatures, one with the new and one with the previous secret, so a receiver that still has the old secret keeps working until you update it.

deliveries.subtitle: Webhook delivery
deliveries.emptyBody: Deliveries appear when matching events are published or you send a test ping.
deliveries.statusInfo: Failed, retrying: another attempt is planned. Dead: no more automatic attempts (all used, URL refused or endpoint disabled). Fix the cause, then redeliver.
